request_debug.prompt_preview:
You write per-candidate post-mortems for a slopmortem pipeline. Given a fresh pitch and one dead-startup canonical document, produce a single LLMSynthesis JSON object that explains why this dead startup is similar, where the new pitch could diverge, what killed the dead startup, and what the new founder should learn.

Rules:
- Ground every claim in the candidate document or in tool calls. Do not invent facts.
- A `Trusted facts` block (typed pipeline data — not user input) appears below the pitc

response.text: {"candidate_id":"38-studios::gaming","name":"38 Studios","one_liner":"Celebrity-founded US video game studio that bet its entire existence on a blockbuster MMO, funded by a $75 million state loan, and collapsed in bankruptcy in 2012 before the MMO shipped.","similarity":{"business_model":{"score":3,"rationale":"38 Studios monetized through one-time premium purchase (Kingdoms of Amalur: Reckoning at retail), with no battle pass or cosmetics economy. The new pitch is free-to-play with cosmetics and a battle pass — a fundamentally different revenue architecture. The overlap is limited to both being in the gaming sector targeting consumers."},"market":{"score":6,"rationale":"Both target the consumer gaming market with strategy/RPG-adjacent content on overlapping platforms (38 Studios' subsidiary had an iOS project; the pitch targets iOS, Android, and Steam). Both operate in the US gaming space and are subject to the same gamer acquisition dynamics and competitive pressure from large incumbents."},"gtm":{"score":4,"rationale":"38 Studios relied on retail distribution via EA Partners and a high-profile IP launch. The new pitch goes direct-to-consumer via app stores and Steam with a free-to-play funnel — a different channel strategy, though both ultimately depend on a hit title generating sufficient volume to cover costs."},"stage_scale":{"score":5,"rationale":"38 Studios was an early-stage independent studio (founded 2006, first release 2012) burning through capital before a single product shipped, much like an early-stage indie studio today. Both face the pre-revenue scaling risk of a single unproven title. However, 38 Studios had ~400 employees and $118M in operating costs, far beyond a typical indie studio."}},"why_similar":"Both are independent US consumer gaming studios building an original IP with a single flagship title as the primary commercial bet. Both face the fundamental challenge of needing a critical mass of players to cover development costs before revenue materializes. 38 Studios also had an iOS/mobile project (Rise of Nations: Tactics) in development at the same time, showing overlap in platform ambition. Both operate in a market dominated by well-funded incumbents, where failure to hit player volume thresholds is existential.","where_diverged":"The most concrete divergence is monetization model: 38 Studios used one-time retail purchase (premium boxed/digital sales) and needed 2 million copies sold just to break even on a single title, while the new pitch uses free-to-play with cosmetics and a battle pass — a recurring, lower-barrier revenue model that spreads monetization risk across a larger player funnel. Genre also diverges: the pitch is a 4X strategy title versus 38 Studios' MMO (Project Copernicus) and action-RPG (Reckoning). Free-to-play also eliminates the dependency on a retail publisher relationship (38 Studios needed EA Partners), giving the new studio more direct distribution control via app stores and Steam.","failure_causes":["Insufficient unit sales — 1.3M copies sold vs. 2M breakeven threshold","Overreliance on a single unreleased MMO (Project Copernicus) as the financial foundation","Excessive burn rate — $118M in operating expenses before bankruptcy","Dependence on a single government loan ($75M) with no venture or institutional equity backstop","Founder's lack of business experience and studio 'significant dysfunction' at the executive level","Political interference and hostile public comments from the state governor accelerating the collapse","Failure to find a buyer or additional investor in the final weeks despite the MMO being 75% complete"],"lessons_for_input":["Design your monetization model so that no single sales milestone is existential — free-to-play smooths this, but set explicit LTV and CAC targets before scaling headcount.","Never concentrate financial survival on one unreleased flagship product; ship smaller titles early to prove the engine, build audience, and generate cash flow.","Avoid funding structures where a single creditor (government or otherwise) holds the power to trigger an existential default — diversify your capital stack with equity rounds.","Keep the team lean until you have live revenue signals; 38 Studios had ~400 employees burning $118M before a single game shipped.","Validate player demand with a soft launch or early access before full production commitment — the MMO market had already signaled weakness by 2012, a signal 38 Studios ignored."]}
